rows.description: My father hugs me and says it is okay to cry. I feel less alone. I learn that being sad is normal and that sharing it makes the load lighter.
My dog has died and I cannot stop crying. The hole in my chest is real grief. Crying, talking and making a small memory box are healthy ways to say goodbye.
I think I could have done something to save my pet. Children often blame themselves, but this is not my fault. Talking to an adult helps me see that I loved my pet well.

rows.subtopic: Parents pressure on career or marriage
rows.description: You love your parents and feel the weight of their sacrifice. Wise: honour the gratitude without treating it as a debt that erases your choices. Immature: obeying while resenting, or rebelling just to prove a point.

rows.subtopic: Parents pressure on career or marriage
rows.description: They compare your marks or salary with relatives. Wise: tell them it hurts, and remember comparison shows their anxiety more than your value. Immature: hating the cousins.

rows.subtopic: Parents pressure on career or marriage
rows.description: You disagree yet respect their experience. Wise: seek their reasons, differ politely, and decide as an adult who owns the outcome. Immature: dismissing them or hiding everything.

rows.subtopic: Parents pressure on career or marriage
rows.description: You see your parents as flawed humans, not heroes. Wise: mourn the illusion and accept them as imperfect people who did their best. Immature: contempt or dismissal of everything they say.
We compete fiercely yet admire each other's work. Wise: let rivalry push both of us. Harmful: denying the friendship for fear of looking soft.
A rival got the captain spot or top rank I wanted and I feel it in my stomach. Wise: admit the envy, study what they did well, and keep working. Harmful: sabotage or spreading doubts.
A rival sneers that I only got in through favour. It stings, especially if I fear it is true. Wise: let my work answer, ask a mentor for honest feedback, and avoid feeding the argument.
I cannot stand even hearing their name. Wise: see how my hate is tying my energy to them and shift my focus to my own goals. Harmful: plotting to hurt their reputation.
I watched someone be insulted for his background and said nothing. I feel guilty. Wise: check on him afterwards, back him up next time, or report. Harmful: excusing my silence as "not my business".
I catch myself assuming things about someone because of his religion or region. Wise: notice the thought without shame, test it against real individuals, and learn. Harmful: denying my own bias.

A coworker makes a casual joke about my caste, religion, region or accent. I feel heat and shame. Wise: name it calmly, note it, use HR or a trusted senior; the fault lies in the joke, not my identity.

A landlord refuses to rent to me because of who I am. I feel angry and small. Wise: it says more about his prejudice; know the legal options, keep notes, find allies and other options. Harmful: internalising it.
My friend says if you were a real friend you would let me copy. That is guilt-tripping. I can say I am your friend and I will help you learn. A friendship that needs cheating is shaky.
A friend asks me to lend homework to copy, and I want to help. Real help is explaining it, not handing over answers. I can say I will teach you. Saying yes to everything to be liked hurts us both.
I lend my friend my colours when she forgot hers and expect nothing. Small generosity builds trust. If she never returns them, I can politely ask. Kindness with boundaries is healthy.
One classmate is nice only when she needs something from me. I feel used. Wise: say no without explaining too much and notice who is kind without a reason. Friends do not only take.

A false rumour about me spreads. My instinct is to explode or vanish. Wise: stay calm, tell parents or a teacher, correct it once with facts, and lean on real friends. Harmful: spreading counter-rumours.
A friend said something harsh in the group and I want to blast them back. Wise: pause, take it to a private chat, and say what hurt. Harmful: public retaliation that everyone screenshots.
I join in mocking someone because everyone is laughing and I fear being next. Wise: notice how easily I slide into cruelty and stop or send the person a kind private message.
